items.claim: The row's apparatus work inside its own span is asymmetric — it engages one of the two variant-note verses it covers, attributes the segment marks to the wrong witness, and leaves a two-site catchword hooking across its rear edge undisclosed.
items.evidence: The onset splice matches its source bytes exactly at the verse it cites (byte tier): הִנֵּ֤ה שֵׁם יְהוָה֙ בָּ֣א (oshb:Isa.30.27, byte). The bounds are in fact better supported than argued — an unnoticed inclusio runs the span's own length, בֹּעֵ֣ר (oshb:Isa.30.27, byte) at the onset answered by בֹּעֲרָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.30.33, byte) inside the very clause quoted at the close. The variant-note position claim is byte-true: the doubled pair גַּם הוא הִ֛יא (oshb:Isa.30.33, byte as spliced; the unpointed first member is skeleton grade) stands at the fifth and sixth tokens, well ahead of the verse-final clause נִשְׁמַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ כְּנַ֣חַל גָּפְרִ֔ית בֹּעֲרָ֖ה בָּֽהּ (oshb:Isa.30.33, byte). The defect is that oshb:Isa.30.32, inside the same span, carries its own variant note staged the same way — נִלְחַם בה בָּֽם (byte as spliced; the unpointed first member is skeleton grade) — and is nowhere disclosed; a span that engages one variant note owes the others it covers. Second, the two segment-mark citations are written as web: refs, but that layer is a single scribal witness with no counterpart in the English text, and the identical segment at 30:33 is cited under the MT witness on the other side of this same seam, so the seam pair disagrees about which witness carries it. Third, an undisclosed cross-seam hook: הֶעְמִ֣יק (oshb:Isa.30.33, byte) recurs as הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ (oshb:Isa.31.6, byte); that unpointed letter string is attested in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses), both flanking this rear edge. It does not overturn the cut — a woe onset and a segment mark both fall there, and the two uses are semantically unrelated — but at a seam of this weight it is an owed disclosure.

items.claim: Every Hebrew claim is a full-verse pointed splice that matches its source bytes exactly, and each frame it names is byte-correct in owner, position, and role.
items.evidence: All three quoted runs reach byte tier against their cited verses (oshb:Isa.31.1, oshb:Isa.31.4, oshb:Isa.31.9) — no copy-degradation. ה֣וֹי is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.31.1 (byte), and the title-construct קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.31.1, byte) does stand inside the woe clause itself; it is a genuine title site and not the separate trisagion object. The frame at oshb:Isa.31.4 is correctly owned: כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְהוָ֣ה אֵלַ֡י (byte) names the deity as speaker in the same clause, so this is a divine frame and not one of the human-messenger uses of the same formula elsewhere in the book. נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.31.9, byte) is characterised correctly as a postpositive signature rather than an onset frame, and it is mid-verse, which the row does not overstate. Apparatus disclosure is complete for the span: both in-span segment marks (oshb:Isa.31.3, oshb:Isa.31.9) and the front-seam mark at oshb:Isa.30.33 are cited with type and single witness, the paseq at oshb:Isa.31.4 is tallied as presence and explicitly not as placement, and no variant note falls anywhere in 31:1-31:9. Two disclosure debts fall short of a challenge: the imperative address it names at web:Isa.31.6 is asserted without its pointed form שׁ֗וּבוּ לַאֲשֶׁ֛ר הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ סָרָ֖ה בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.31.6, byte), and the unpointed letter string shared by הֶעְמִ֣יק (oshb:Isa.30.33, byte) and הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ (oshb:Isa.31.6, byte) — exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses) — hooks across this unit's front seam undisclosed. Neither touches the boundary, which the bytes carry on their own.
tier_citations: tier-1 woe onset / divine-frame ownership / postpositive signature

items.claim: The onset rests entirely on the English rendering of a particle the row never quotes, the same verse-initial particle is treated as non-structural elsewhere in this same stretch, and the variant note inside the span is undisclosed.
items.evidence: No Hebrew appears anywhere in this row, yet its whole boundary case is a 'fresh topic onset'. The onset verse opens הֵ֥ן (oshb:Isa.32.1, byte), the presentative particle the English witness renders 'Behold'; with that rendering removed the row is left with a tier-3 single-witness segment mark and a topic description. The particle is verse-initial at exactly 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses), and one of those sites is oshb:Isa.33.7, הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (byte), which within this same stretch of chapters is treated as internal texture rather than as an onset. Driving a boundary on the particle here while denying it there is an inconsistency that is invisible in the English and plain in the Hebrew; the row owes either the pointed form or a different driver. Separately, oshb:Isa.32.7 lies inside this span and carries a variant note staged as the doubled pair ענוים עֲנִיִּים֙ (byte as spliced; the unpointed first member is skeleton grade). The row discloses no variant note at all, and no counting or slicing claim in that verse is admissible without it. What is correct: the segment-mark citations are complete for the span and keep the two mark types distinct (oshb:Isa.32.8 and the front-seam mark at oshb:Isa.31.9, single-witness).

items.claim: The rear edge is placed exactly where the English witness's sentence punctuation falls, with no Hebrew argued, and a three-site token chain runs straight across that edge undisclosed.
items.evidence: The onset is byte-true but unquoted: נָשִׁים֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת קֹ֖מְנָה שְׁמַ֣עְנָה קוֹלִ֑י (oshb:Isa.32.9, byte) carries both the vocative and the second-person feminine plural imperative forms the row names; a form-class claim carrying a boundary owes its pointed form. The rear edge is argued from the two verses forming 'one sentence in the WEB rendering' — a criterion supplied by the English witness's punctuation. In the Hebrew the subordinating עַד יֵ֨עָרֶ֥ה (oshb:Isa.32.15, byte) does open a dependent clause, so the conclusion survives; but the clause chain does not stop where the English full stop falls. וְהָיָ֤ה מִדְבָּר֙ לַכַּרְמֶ֔ל (oshb:Isa.32.15, byte) is continued by וְשָׁכַ֥ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט (oshb:Isa.32.16, byte) in the identical waw-plus-perfect pattern, so the row's own syntactic criterion reads past its own close. Across that close runs שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.32.9, byte), attested at exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses) — oshb:Isa.32.9 and oshb:Isa.32.11, byte-identical to each other, and oshb:Isa.32.18, שַׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת, which matches the first two at skeleton tier only, the accents differing. Two of the three sites are this row's own onset evidence and the third sits beyond its close; a byte-true chain straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed, and it is not disclosed. Correctly handled: the variant note at oshb:Isa.32.15 is disclosed and left unadjudicated, and segment-mark disclosure is complete for the span (oshb:Isa.32.8, single-witness).

items.claim: The front edge is contested by the bytes on three independent counts: the clause chain runs across it, the register change cited to justify it is not located there, and the alternative it rejects is the one the lexical evidence supports.
items.evidence: No Hebrew appears in the row. Its opening verse begins וְשָׁכַ֥ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט (oshb:Isa.32.16, byte) — a waw-plus-perfect continuing וְהָיָ֤ה מִדְבָּר֙ לַכַּרְמֶ֔ל (oshb:Isa.32.15, byte) inside the same subordinate clause; nothing verse-initial marks a fresh start. The English 'Then' at that verse renders the waw form, not an adverb in the text: the Hebrew adverb אָ֥ז (oshb:Isa.35.5, byte) is verse-initial at exactly 6 verses book-wide (sweep: 6 verses), and oshb:Isa.32.16 is not among them. The two key nouns cross the edge chiastically — מִדְבָּר֙ לַכַּרְמֶ֔ל וכרמל וְהַכַּרְמֶ֖ל (oshb:Isa.32.15, byte) then בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה בַּכַּרְמֶ֥ל (oshb:Isa.32.16, byte). Second, the stated ground, that the second-person plural address drops after web:Isa.32.15, is not where the bytes put it: the last second-person address forms are חִרְדוּ֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת רְגָ֖זָה בֹּֽטְח֑וֹת פְּשֹׁ֣טָֽה וְעֹ֔רָה וַחֲג֖וֹרָה (oshb:Isa.32.11, byte); the verse the row names carries the first-person plural עָלֵ֛ינוּ (oshb:Isa.32.15, byte); and the intervening verses carry no second-person form in either witness's rendering — the participle סֹֽפְדִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.32.12, byte) is rendered as an imperative by the English witness alone. The register change therefore falls at least four verses ahead of the cut it is used to justify. Third, the rejected alternative of holding web:Isa.32.9-Isa.32.20 as one span is what the lexical evidence supports: שַׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.32.18, byte) rejoins the token opening the rejected span's first and third verses (exactly 3 verses book-wide, sweep: 3 verses; skeleton tier across the three, byte-identical between the first two), and מִבְטַחִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.32.18, byte; 1 verse book-wide, sweep: 1 verse) answers בֹּֽטח֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.32.9, byte; that spelling at exactly 3 verses book-wide, sweep: 3 verses) on the same root — a root-level observation across two distinct attested spellings, not a token match. The closing formula is byte-true but unquoted: אַשְׁרֵיכֶ֕ם (oshb:Isa.32.20, byte); and the single tier-3 segment mark cited at that close (single-witness) corroborates a break there equally well under the grouping the row rejected, so it cannot arbitrate between them.

items.claim: The negative that carries this whole-chapter extent — that no comparable onset interrupts before the next chapter's summons — is byte-false immediately after both interior segment marks the row dismisses.
items.evidence: Credit first: both quoted runs reach byte tier at their cited verses, ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד (oshb:Isa.33.1, byte) is verse-initial, the sixth-of-six digit for the woe onsets across these chapters is correct against the byte evidence (sweep: 6 verses), and the speech form at oshb:Isa.33.10 is correctly read as a signature rather than a narrative or messenger onset. The interior claim is where it fails. Directly after the segment mark the row dismisses at oshb:Isa.33.12, the next verse opens שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי וּדְע֥וּ קְרוֹבִ֖ים גְּבֻרָתִֽי (oshb:Isa.33.13, byte) — a verse-initial imperative summons with paired addressees. That imperative stands verse-initial at exactly 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses), the book's own hear-summons class, and at exactly 1 verse across chapters 28-35 (sweep: 1 verse) — this one. It is the same formal class as the summons the row credits as the next unit's onset, קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (oshb:Isa.34.1, byte). Directly after the other dismissed mark at oshb:Isa.33.6, the next verse opens הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.33.7, byte) — the same verse-initial presentative particle (18 verses book-wide, sweep: 18 verses) that is used as an onset driver at oshb:Isa.32.1 within this same stretch. And the petition the row itself names begins יְהוָ֥ה חָנֵּ֖נוּ (oshb:Isa.33.2, byte), a vocative plus imperative, so the row's own summary of its contents contradicts its negative. None of this compels a cut on its own — the segment layer is single-witness tier-3 corroboration and never a driver, and absence of a mark is never counterevidence. What fails is the stated ground: a whole-chapter extent is carried by a negative asserted precisely where the bytes carry the markers it denies.

items.claim: The row's own onset class recurs verse-initially inside the span at an undisclosed site, no Hebrew is quoted anywhere, and the whole-chapter extent is carried at the top confidence band.
items.evidence: No Hebrew is quoted. The onset it argues is byte-true — קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (oshb:Isa.34.1, byte), verse-initial imperatives with their vocatives, the imperative standing verse-initial at exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses) — but it is argued only through the English rendering. The negative that carries the span's extent is contested at oshb:Isa.34.16, which opens דִּרְשׁ֨וּ מֵֽעַל סֵ֤פֶר יְהוָה֙ וּֽקְרָ֔אוּ (byte): a verse-initial imperative pair addressing a fresh audience, the imperative standing verse-initial at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses), the other site elsewhere in the book. That site carries no vocative, so it is formally weaker than the row's own onset and I do not claim it forces a cut; but the row's negative is written to exclude comparable onsets, and this is the same imperative-onset class it uses for itself, so it is owed a disclosure either way. Apparatus disclosure is otherwise complete and correctly typed: the closing segment mark at oshb:Isa.34.17 (single-witness), and no variant note and no paseq site falls anywhere in this chapter. One further exposure: a span of whole-chapter extent is carried at the top confidence band, above the cap this campaign sets for spans of that extent, and the unaddressed interior onset above is exactly the kind of exposure that cap exists for.

items.claim: The rejected alternative turns on one English adverb doing two different jobs, with no counterpart in the Hebrew, and a second imperative onset inside the span goes unnamed.
items.evidence: No Hebrew is quoted. The row declines a cut at web:Isa.35.5 on the ground that the 'then' formula there merely resumes as an earlier 'then' did at web:Isa.32.16. In the Hebrew these are not the same object. אָ֥ז stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.35.5 (byte) and again as אָ֣ז at oshb:Isa.35.6 (byte) — two adjacent sites, not the single site the row treats — and that adverb is verse-initial at exactly 6 verses book-wide (sweep: 6 verses), none of them oshb:Isa.32.16, which opens instead with the waw-plus-perfect וְשָׁכַ֥ן (byte). The parallel is an artifact of one English word rendering two different Hebrew constructions, and it is the sole support offered for declining that cut. Second, the row names one internal imperative address at web:Isa.35.3 but not the second: oshb:Isa.35.4 opens אִמְרוּ֙ לְנִמְהֲרֵי לֵ֔ב (byte) and carries the presentative הִנֵּ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ (byte) — the same particle class treated as an onset driver elsewhere in this stretch — so the row's own account of its internal texture is incomplete. What it gets right: segment-mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed for the span, the interior mark at oshb:Isa.35.2 and the closing mark at oshb:Isa.35.10 (single-witness), no variant note or paseq site falls in this chapter, and it stops at the frame seam without crossing it, where the following verse opens with a narrative onset in the bytes. Exposure: a span of whole-chapter extent is carried at the top confidence band, above the cap set for spans of that extent.
